column2: Kish's chain through Abiel, Sared, Bachir and Aphek to a Benjaminite man remains, followed by mighty man. The selected ancestral names are not replaced by familiar alternate genealogies.
Saul's height, goodness and superiority among Israel's sons remain, with shoulders upward and all the land as the comparative frame.
column3: Good for agathos is provisional; physical attractiveness may be implicated by the context without exhaustively defining moral character.

column2: Lost donkeys motivate Kish's singular instruction to take one servant followed by plural arise/go/seek; both of you makes the change of addressees audible.
The route through Ephraim, Selcha, Easakem and Jakim retains repeated traversals and failures, including the distinct there was nothing clause.
At Siph, Saul proposes return lest his father abandon concern for the donkeys and worry about us; plural concern includes the servant.
Behold, the renowned man of God and emphatic certainty of his words motivate the servant's proposal to learn about their traveled way. The journey is not changed to an unrelated future itinerary.

Propose Behold, we will go in place of If we go: the selected text has a presentative and future assertion, not an explicit conditional. The question, exhausted loaves, containers and absence of further possessions remain.
column3: The reply can be heard as considering a plan, but English if unnecessarily recasts its grammatical form; the short assertion followed by a question preserves that deliberative context.

column2: The servant answers again, presents the quarter-shekel in his hand and tells Saul you will give it; the giving subject is not changed to the servant himself.
The explanatory aside preserves each person's former invitation and the people's former term seer for prophet. Its historical framing remains separate from the current dialogue.
Saul approves the word, invites departure and goes with the servant to the man's city; the verbal agreement and ensuing action remain distinct.
Ascent to the city leads to meeting girls drawing water and the question whether the seer is here; no identification is supplied before their reply.
The girls affirm presence, point ahead and explain today's arrival and sacrifice at Bama; the repeated day expressions remain despite the unusual now for the day construction.
The seer is to be found before ascending to Bama; emphatic non-eating until his entry, blessing the sacrifice, guests eating afterward and the renewed command all remain.
column3: The temporal expression during the day is provisional and not expanded into a precise appointment time.

column2: As the men enter the city's interior, there was Samuel preserves the presentative encounter before his ascent to Bama. The destination remains a transliterated name.
The Lord's uncovering Samuel's ear occurs one day before Saul's coming; the bodily revelation image and exact relative day remain.
Tomorrow's sending, anointing as ruler, saving from foreigners, divine regard for humiliation and the cry reaching God remain in their causal order.
Samuel sees Saul and the Lord answers with a presentative identification and the ruler's task among My people; Here is carries idou naturally.
Saul approaches in the city interior and requests the seer's house; please expresses the request particle without altering ordinary human address.
I am he identifies Samuel, who commands ascent and eating, promises morning dismissal and disclosure of everything in Saul's heart. No information is specified beyond that promise.
The third-day lost donkeys, prohibition on setting his heart on them, their discovery and Israel's beautiful things belonging to Saul and his father's house remain.
column3: Beautiful things for horaia is provisional; it is not replaced without evidence by all Israel's desire, and the three-day idiom is not a modern chronological calculation.

column2: Saul identifies his small tribal division and smallest clan within Benjamin, then asks why such a word was spoken to him. Tribal hierarchy is rendered contextually rather than as literal sceptres.
Samuel includes the young servant, gives both a place among the first invitees and preserves about seventy men. No replacement with thirty guests is made.
Samuel asks the cook for the portion he previously gave with instructions to set it aside; the repeated giving and keeping establish the meal's preparation.
The haunch, remaining portion, instruction to eat, testimony apart from the others and gnawing command all remain before Saul eats with Samuel.
column3: The phrase about testimony and apoknize remain lexical questions; the text is not rewritten as a standard reserved-for-this-occasion formula.

column2: The singular descent from Bama precedes unnamed plural people spreading bedding for Saul on the roof; bedding supplies the object implied by the spreading verb.
column3: The subject of descended is not explicitly named in this unit; the inherited he leaves that connection open.

column2: Sleeping remains at the start of this unit, followed by rising dawn, Samuel's roof call, Saul's rising and both going outside. No nighttime conversation is inserted.
The descent toward the city's side precedes a command to send the young man ahead and the emphatic you to stand and hear God's word; But distinguishes the two men's instructions.
column3: A while renders hos semeron provisionally; no exact duration is claimed.

column2: Oil flask, pouring, kiss, anointing question, rule, surrounding enemies, rescue and the full sign introduction remain. The longer selected commission is not shortened to a familiar form.

Propose restoring Behold before the father's changed concern and specifying you both in the later plural phrase as well as the donkey search. Rachel's plural tombs, two leaping men and lavish expenditure remain.
column3: Leaping greatly and lavish expenditure retain difficult selected readings; they are not changed to a place-name and anxiety respectively.

column2: Tabor's oak and three men ascending to God at Bethel remain, with three goats, three containers of loaves and one wine skin distributed among the men.
Inquiry about welfare precedes two first portions of loaves and acceptance from their hand; first portions preserves aparchai rather than simply counting two unspecified loaves.
God's hill, the foreigners' station, Nasib the foreigner, plural you both entering, prophetic chorus, Bama and all four instruments remain.
column3: Station for anastema and Nasib's identity remain open; nabla and kinyra are preserved without asserting modern instrument equivalences.

column2: The Lord's Spirit leaps upon Saul, he prophesies with the group and is changed into another man; the active divine arrival and passive transformation remain.
The signs precede the instruction to do everything his hand finds because God is with him; the causal grounding and hand image remain explicit.
Propose restoring the presentative Behold before Samuel's announced descent. Before Gilgal, whole burnt offering, peace sacrifices, seven-day waiting and subsequent instruction remain.
column3: Before Gilgal follows the selected wording rather than silently changing it to before me to Gilgal; future English will come expresses the announced impending action of the Greek present.

column2: Saul turns his shoulder to depart, God changes his heart to another heart, and all signs arrive that day; the repeated change language is retained.
Propose restoring behold when the prophetic chorus faces him. The movement to the hill, Spirit's leap and Saul's prophesying among them remain in sequence.

Propose retaining the explicit presentative after the seeing: they saw, and behold, he was among the prophets. Before renders the yesterday-and-third-day idiom; both questions about Kish's son and Saul among prophets remain.
One person's question is whose father he has, singular his, followed by the repeated Saul proverb; the question is not changed to their father.
Saul finishes prophesying and comes to the hill; the selected repeated hill destination is not harmonized into a different location.
His relative addresses both Saul and the servant; their plural answer retains searching, failure to find and coming to Samuel.
column3: Relative renders oikeios without specifying uncle where the Greek does not.

column2: The relative asks Saul specifically for what Samuel said to him; please carries the request particle and singular focus remains recoverable.
Plainly told conveys the emphatic reporting expression; the discovered donkeys are reported but the kingship word withheld. The withholding is not attributed to a stated motive.
Samuel summons all the people to the Lord at Mizpah; both divine destination and earthly assembly place remain.
The Lord's first-person recollection includes Egypt, Pharaoh king of Egypt and every oppressive kingdom; the repeated deliverance scope is not reduced to Egypt alone.
Today's contempt for the saving God, all evils and distresses, the emphatic refusal and demand for a king, then standing by tribes and clans remain.
column3: Quotation boundaries are editorial: ordinary You in the reported demand treats Samuel as its addressee in light of chapter 8; the Greek itself does not supply modern nested quotation marks.

column2: All tribes are brought near and Benjamin selected by lot; the selection verb supports lot rather than a vote or military appointment.
Benjamin's clans, Mattari, its men and Saul are selected in descending order; the failed search remains singular in the selected text.
column3: He looked for him leaves the unnamed searching agent unresolved; Samuel is contextually plausible, but no explicit source name is claimed.

column2: Samuel inquires again whether the man is coming here; the Lord's behold introduces hiding among baggage. The question is not rewritten as whether another man remains.
A singular actor runs, takes Saul and stations him among the people; Saul's height above the people's shoulders remains.
column3: The fetching actor is not explicitly named; the inherited he preserves the source's compressed agency rather than silently changing to plural runners.

column2: Samuel asks about the Lord's choice for Himself and Saul's uniqueness; the people's acknowledgement and wish that the king live remain distinct.
The king's claim is spoken, written in a scroll and placed before the Lord, followed by dismissal and each person's departure.
column3: Claim for dikaioma remains consistent with chapter 8 but provisional; no identity of the written document or later legal code is supplied.

column2: Saul's return to Gibeah includes sons of might whose hearts the Lord touched; their accompaniment retains divine initiative rather than merely political loyalty.
Pestilent men question Saul's ability to save, dishonor him and withhold gifts. No concluding silence response is added from a different textual form.
